title: Trajectory Contract Fixture
description: One contract fixture: an HTTP scenario the runner plays against an implementation. Copyright 2026 Athion, Inc. Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0. This schema documents the shape for readers in any language; runner/src/load.mjs (lintFixture) is the executable check and must list the same required keys.

test_id.description: Unique id and the file name prefix: the file is <test_id>-<slug>.json. Prefixes: agt- (agent action), rly- (outbound-only relay), prm- (permission), aud- (audit trail), cfg- (config connector).

name.description: Plain-English statement of what the fixture checks.

category.description: The contract this fixture belongs to; also the directory it lives in.

level.description: MUST: a failure fails the run. SHOULD: a failure is reported as a note. IMPL-DEFINED: allowed variance, reported as a note. EXTENSION:<name>: skipped unless the target declares the extension.

source.description: Where the requirement comes from, for example "REST-05" (a docs/REST_Protocol.md section) or "C-AUD-3" (a contract clause). Required when level is MUST or SHOULD.

tags.description: Free-form tags for filtering, for example "invoke", "sse", "live".

requires.description: Capabilities, roles and extensions the target must declare for this fixture to run; otherwise it is skipped. Every {{roles.X}} placeholder in the fixture must name X here, or a capability listed here must imply it (see CAPABILITY_ROLES in runner/src/load.mjs). environment_oid is always available.

attests.description: A clause id (for example "C-RLY-4") that cannot be observed over HTTP. The runner does not run the fixture's steps (keep steps empty): when the target's attestations map has the clause set to true the result is note with reason "attested: <clause> ..."; otherwise it is skip. Never a pass.

setup.description: Steps run before the checked steps. Their expectations are not graded unless they fail outright.

steps.description: The checked steps. Each step's expect block is graded at the fixture's level.

expected.description: Reserved. Not evaluated by the runner; only each step's expect block is graded.

teardown.description: Steps run after the checked steps, even on failure. Usually marked tolerate: true.

step.description: One step. Placeholders: {{roles.X}} (from the target's roles map), {{uniq}} (a per-run unique token), {{name}} (a value captured by an earlier step).

kind.description: request: one HTTP call. wait_state: poll an instance until it reaches one of the states. sse_read: read SSE frames for a bounded time. capture: pull values out of an earlier response.

id.description: Optional label; a capture step refers to an earlier request step by its id.

from.description: For capture steps: the id of the request step whose response to read.

path.description: Path relative to the target's base_url (or probe_url when probe is true).

probe.description: Send this request to probe_url instead of base_url.

auth.description: false omits the target's auth header on this request (for unauthenticated-call fixtures). Default true.

capture.description: name -> JSONPath into the response body; the value becomes {{name}} for later steps.

tolerate.description: Do not fail the fixture if this step errors (used in teardown).

instance.description: Instance id for wait_state and sse_read.

states.description: States that satisfy a wait_state step.

timeout_s.description: Per-step override of the target's wait_s / sse_s.

last_event_id.description: sse_read: sent as the Last-Event-ID header to resume a stream.

max.description: sse_read: stop after this many events.

until_state.description: sse_read: stop after a state_change into one of these states.

capture_events.description: sse_read: name of the var that receives the events array. The step's response body is {events, ended} where ended is count | state | timeout | end, so expect and capture can read $.events and $.ended.

expect.description: Expectations on a response. See runner/src/assert.mjs.

status.description: An integer, or {one_of: [..], note_if: {one_of: [..] | range: [lo, hi]}} where note_if statuses give a note instead of a failure.

json.description: Checks on the JSON body. path is a small JSONPath subset: $, .key, [n], [-n] (from the end), [*]. Values in the item (equals, in, where.equals, ...) may use {{var}} placeholders; they are resolved from captured variables before grading.

path.description: JSONPath relative to each element reached by path (starts with $).

where.description: Keeps only the elements reached by path whose relative where.path yields exactly where.equals. Applied before select and the operators.

select.description: JSONPath relative to each (kept) element; the operators then grade what it reaches.

not_equals.description: Fails when the value at path deeply equals this (for example a captured {{first_iid}}). Nothing at the path is a failure, as for equals.

headers.description: Checks on response headers, keyed by header name.
